The field-valued row is established; these sources do not by themselves verify the full big-fppf relative group-scheme row for arbitrary test bases.
present_status: As of November 2026: The pointwise calculation is established and the relative derivation is conditional on its explicitly specified vanishing theorem. Do not equate the full group-scheme row with its perfected realization.

statement: A polynomial algebra in n variables over a field, localized at a maximal ideal, is a regular local ring of dimension n.
status_on_pages: proof sketched in wholly cancelled draft
computation: computations.md §23 gives the dimension/depth formula and variable-count check.
fate: Stacks00OO Lemma10.114.1 and Prop10.114.2 give a complete proof over every field, using successive minimal polynomials of residue coordinates; no perfectness assumption is needed. The t₀ versus t₁ reading changes the number of variables.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with the literal variable count fixed; the draft’s residue-field reduction is compressed and is not silently extended to inseparable base-change arguments.

statement: For a noetherian local A and a prime P of A[t₁,…,t_n] lying above its maximal ideal, dim(A[t]_P)=dim A+dim(κ(m)[t]_{̅P}); the fibre term is n−trdegκ(P)/κ(m). For a maximal ideal over m the transcendence degree is0.
computation: computations.md §23.
fate: Stacks00OG Lemma10.112.7 proves dimS=dimR+dim(closed fibre) for flat noetherian local maps. Stacks00OO gives the polynomial-fibre dimension; the residue-transcendence version is the standard finite-type dimension formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established reconstructed formula; the two statements coincide when M is genuinely maximal.

statement: For the flat local polynomial localization with regular closed fibre of dimension ν, depth B_P=depth A+ν, hence dimension−depth is unchanged.
status_on_pages: stated without proof in cancelled draft; final equality incomplete
computation: computations.md §23 derives the subtraction.
fate: Stacks0338 Lemma10.163.1 proves the flat local depth formula and explicitly attributes it to EGAIV2 Cor6.3.1. Together with CL-SA19-101 this gives the coprofondness identity. The exact EGAIV2 original locator was followed through the verified Stacks proof; its separate PDF was not read here.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established under the noetherian, finite-module and flatness hypotheses.

statement: The cancelled final corollary proposes ascent of an unspecified list of properties under polynomial extension/localization.
computation: No numerical computation is used; the logical/formal check is described in the statement and fate.
fate: EGAIV3 and Stacks0338 support concrete regular/Cohen–Macaulay/depth consequences, but the blank property list prevents identifying the proposed universal claim. No source can fill this blank solely from neighboring words.
present_status: As of November 2026: Not a definite theorem; plausible examples are reconstructions, not restored text.

statement: For a flat ring map A→B, faithful flatness is equivalent to surjectivity on spectra, nonzero fibres at maximal ideals, faithful tensoring and injectivity of every module’s unit map. Faithful flatness implies contraction IB∩A=I; conversely contraction of all proper ideals plus flatness gives faithful flatness.
computation: computations.md §24 gives the unit-map and ideal-contraction proofs.
fate: Stacks00HP Lemma10.39.15 and the surrounding Stacks00H9 section prove the fibre/faithful-flatness criteria. SGA1 ExposéVIII develops faithfully-flat descent. The page’s B h(A) is a quotient-reading alarm.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established; flatness is essential in the equivalence list.

statement: Softness asks that sections over suitable closed subsets extend; a nontrivial constant sheaf on a connected space can fail it when a disconnected closed subset carries different prescribed values.
status_on_pages: definition and example in reused typescript
computation: computations.md §21 tests X=[0,1],closed subset{0,1},values0 and1.
fate: Grothendieck1957 §3.3 p159 discusses soft/flasque sheaves and their acyclicity; Cartan1951XV develops the related fine-sheaf machinery. The manuscript uses local versions of extension axioms, so a global softness claim requires the stated separation/paracompactness hypotheses.
present_status: As of November 2026: The extension obstruction is elementary; the exact typed textbook provenance remains unidentified.

statement: A soft sheaf of rings on a paracompact Hausdorff space admits a partition of unity subordinate to a locally finite open refinement, using local extension of1 and support control.
status_on_pages: proof fragment, continuing beyond supplied face
computation: computations.md §21 gives a complete locally finite recursive construction.
fate: Cartan1951XV §§5–6 proves the classical fine/partition-of-unity framework, including the ring of arbitrary functions; Grothendieck1957 §3.3 supplies soft-sheaf extensions. The exact maximal-family continuation is absent, so the full general soft-ring argument is separately reconstructed in computations.md rather than claimed read on the sheet.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established in the stated paracompact Hausdorff setting; not a theorem on arbitrary spaces or merely local softness without its globalization hypotheses.

statement: If I is the sheaf of arbitrary integer-valued functions, F→F⊗_Z I is a monomorphism. At each stalk evaluation at the base point splits the map; the resulting tensor sheaf is fine in the standard paracompact setting.
status_on_pages: proof sketched across reversed typed-page order
computation: computations.md §21 gives the stalk splitting and the alternative primitive-element torsion-free lemma.
fate: Cartan1951XV §5 Prop1 and§6 prove tensor preservation of fineness and fineness of the arbitrary-function ring; Cartan1951XVI p4 gives precisely the tensor embedding into a fine sheaf. The independent stalk retraction checks the actual arrow without demanding a global retraction.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established before the likely manuscript period. Exact typed provenance is not inferred merely from the theorem match.

statement: A fine sheaf on an open or closed subspace remains fine after the appropriate extension by zero to X; the local support endomorphisms extend by zero.
computation: computations.md §21 checks supports and the locally finite sum after extension.
fate: Cartan1951XV §§5–6 gives the local-support endomorphism definition; its pointwise extension proves the assertion with the chosen open j_! or closed i_* convention. This is distinct from a claim that all cohomology of the extension vanishes in the exotic relative curve site.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established for the standard topological sheaf setting and the stated extension functor.

his_statement: torsion-free H; a primitive; x↦x⊗a injective
statement: If H is a torsion-free abelian group and a is nonzero and not divisible by any integer of absolute value>1 in H, then G→G⊗_Z H, x↦x⊗a, is injective for every abelian group G.
status_on_pages: proof given across reversed typed-page order
computation: computations.md §21 gives both the finite-subgroup argument and the evaluation splitting in the actual application.
fate: The finitely generated case follows because a primitive vector extends to a Z-basis; passage through finitely generated subgroups gives the general case. The specific sheaf application is also in Cartan1951XVI p4. This is an algebraic proof, not an inference that every nonzero element of a torsion-free group is primitive.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established with the primitive-element condition exactly retained.

his_statement: if G fine then F⊗G fine
statement: Tensoring a fine sheaf of abelian groups with any sheaf preserves fineness, since its support-controlled endomorphisms act on the second factor.
computation: computations.md §21 checks the support and identity conditions.
fate: Cartan1951XV §5 Prop1 states and proves this tensor property. The proof applies1⊗θ to each fine endomorphism; local finiteness and the identity sum are preserved.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established classical fine-sheaf construction.

statement: For a flat ring map A→B, faithful flatness is equivalent to injectivity of A→B together with flatness of the A-module B/A.
computation: computations.md §24 gives the Tor argument.
fate: Stacks00H9 gives faithful flatness and pure module-unit maps. The Tor exact sequence for0→A→B→B/A→0 proves the equivalence: Tor₁(B/A,M) is the kernel of M→B⊗M.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established after recognizing the quotient; B h(A) is not a meaningful substitute in this exact sequence.
